recall_prompt: Say how you would find the conjugate of this product — what you do first, and what a conjugate changes.
insider_note: The order is fixed: multiply to one number a + ib, then flip only the sign of the i part. The product 18 − i is not the answer — the question asks for its conjugate, 18 + i, and stopping one line early loses the second mark.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Multiply out
steps.margin_note: First mark. Multiply first, then take the conjugate — a conjugate of a product needs the product as one number a + ib.

recall.must_convey: That the product is expanded and simplified with i² = −1 to 18 − i.

steps.why: A conjugate flips the sign of the imaginary part of ONE number, so the product has to be a single a + ib before the flip. (Taking conjugates of each factor first also works, but the exam expects the product.)
common_mistakes: Missing a cross term and getting 6 − 12i².

steps.label: Take the conjugate
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Conjugate = same real part, opposite sign on the i part. 18 − i becomes 18 + i.
lines: The conjugate of a + ib is a − ib.

recall.must_convey: That the conjugate changes the sign of the imaginary part, so the conjugate of 18 − i is 18 + i.
accept: change the sign of the imaginary part, the conjugate of eighteen minus i is eighteen plus i
the answer is eighteen plus i

steps.why: The conjugate is the mirror image across the real axis: the real part stays, the imaginary part changes sign. That is the entire definition, and it is applied once.
common_mistakes: Changing the sign of the real part too, giving −18 + i.
Stopping at 18 − i, the product, without writing its conjugate.
